advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Compute `_result_detail(result, target.kind)` once into a local and branch on that value in `_probe_registry`.
evidence: src/rebar/grounding/terraform_source.py:267: `if _result_detail(result, target.kind) is not None:`
src/rebar/grounding/terraform_source.py:271: `_result_detail(result, target.kind),`
`_metadata_detail` calls `json.loads(body.decode("utf-8"))` each invocation (terraform_source.py:358)
advisory.finding: `_result_detail(result, target.kind)` is computed twice in `_probe_registry` (once for the truthiness guard, once to pass the value), so on any registry response the JSON body is decoded/parsed twice via `_metadata_detail`.
advisory.suggested_fix: detail = _result_detail(result, target.kind); if detail is not None: return session._abstain(..., detail, ...)

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Map the generic `except OSError` fallback in `_safe_network_probe` to a network/other reason distinct from `dns_error` (e.g. reuse `_url_error_detail`-style classification or a `registry_server_error`/generic network detail).
evidence: src/rebar/grounding/terraform_source.py:320: `    except OSError:`
src/rebar/grounding/terraform_source.py:321: `        return None, "dns_error"`
`socket.gaierror` (the true DNS error) is already caught separately at terraform_source.py:312
advisory.finding: The catch-all `except OSError: return None, "dns_error"` in `_safe_network_probe` labels every non-URLError OS-level transport failure (e.g. connection refused/reset, EHOSTUNREACH) as `dns_error`, which is a misleading closed reason for failures that are not name-resolution errors.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm with the security overlay whether literal-IP-only target validation is sufficient, or whether resolved-address (private-range) filtering is required before the metadata GET.
evidence: src/rebar/grounding/terraform_source.py:223: `return host.rsplit(".", 1)[-1].lower() in _PRIVATE_TLDS`
`_valid_host` rejects only parseable literal IPs (terraform_source.py:229-231)
ADR 0115 §5 scopes the guard to 'literal IPs' — a documented boundary, not literal DNS resolution
advisory.finding: Target validation rejects only LITERAL IP hosts and known private-use TLDs; a custom registry hostname that resolves to a private/internal IP (e.g. `registry.internal-corp.io`) is treated as a public target and probed uncredentialed, so DNS-rebinding / internal-name SSRF is not covered by the target policy.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that drives the REAL `_https_probe` (not the mocked seam) against a redirect-issuing stub server/handler and asserts the opener does NOT follow the 3xx and no `Authorization` header reaches the redirect target.
evidence: src/rebar/grounding/terraform_source.py:55 `class _NoRedirect(urllib.request.HTTPRedirectHandler): def redirect_request(...): return None`
src/rebar/grounding/terraform_source.py:72 `opener = urllib.request.build_opener(_NoRedirect)`
tests/unit/grounding/test_terraform_source.py:96 `monkeypatch.setattr(ts, "_https_probe", fake)` — the seam containing `_NoRedirect` is mocked in every network test
search: `_NoRedirect` has (no matches) in the test file
test docstring at line 476 claims 'the token is NEVER carried to the redirect target (the helper does not follow it)' but line 478-479 fakes a 302 HttpResult return, so the real opener never runs
advisory.finding: The no-redirect enforcement (`_NoRedirect` opener via `build_opener`) added in `_https_probe` — the mechanism that implements the diff's 'cross-host redirect is network_error BEFORE the credential is sent / token NEVER carried to the redirect target' security contract — is never exercised: every network test monkeypatches `_https_probe` (line 96), and `_NoRedirect` has zero test references. `test_cross_host_redirect_is_network_error_before_credential` injects a synthetic 302 `HttpResult` and only asserts `_result_detail`'s status->reason mapping, so a refactor that removed `_NoRedirect` (letting the real opener follow the redirect and forward the `Authorization: Bearer` header to the attacker host) would leave the test green. Regression-blind for the specific security behavior this diff introduces.
scenarios: A behavior-preserving-looking refactor drops `_NoRedirect` or passes it wrongly to `build_opener`, so the live opener follows a registry's cross-host 3xx and forwards the Bearer token to the redirect host — all current tests still pass.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test using an actual `urllib.request` HTTP fixture (e.g. a localhost `http.server`/wsgiref handler issuing a 302 to a second host) that calls `ts._https_probe(...)` directly and asserts the returned `HttpResult.status == 302` (unfollowed) and that a second request/host was never contacted, exercising `_NoRedirect` and `build_opener`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that drives the real `_https_probe` against a stub server returning a body larger than `MAX_METADATA_BYTES` and asserts `OversizedMetadata` propagates from `_https_probe` itself.
evidence: src/rebar/grounding/terraform_source.py:73 `body = _read_capped(resp, max_bytes)` inside the mocked `_https_probe`
tests/unit/grounding/test_terraform_source.py:384 oversized test raises `ts.OversizedMetadata` from the responder, bypassing `_https_probe`'s own read
tests/unit/grounding/test_terraform_source.py:461 `_read_capped(_CappedFP(big), ...)` drives the helper directly, not through `_https_probe`
advisory.finding: The live-response body capping in `_https_probe` (calling `_read_capped` on the real `resp`/`exc` file objects) is not exercised end-to-end: the oversized-metadata network test raises `OversizedMetadata` from the mocked seam (line 384-386) rather than returning an oversized body through the real `_https_probe`, and the `_read_capped` unit tests (line 458, 466) drive a `_CappedFP` stand-in directly. No test proves `_https_probe` actually invokes `_read_capped` with `MAX_METADATA_BYTES` on a real response, so a refactor removing the cap call inside `_https_probe` would not be caught.
scenarios: `_https_probe` is refactored to `resp.read()` without the cap; an oversized real response is no longer bounded, but tests stay green because they mock the seam or call `_read_capped` in isolation.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve the target hostname and reject it (abstain rejected_target) when any resolved address is loopback/link-local/private/reserved, closing the DNS-to-internal SSRF gap in probe_source.
evidence: `_valid_host` only rejects literal IPs (`ipaddress.ip_address(host.strip("[]"))`), <2-label hosts, and per-label charset — no resolved-address check (terraform_source.py:226-246)
`_is_private_host` inspects only `host.rsplit(".",1)[-1]` against `_PRIVATE_TLDS` — a literal-TLD test, not the resolved IP (terraform_source.py:221-223)

`_probe_registry` attaches a credential and probes any host that passes `_credential_for_host`/`_is_private_host`; the endpoint host is taken verbatim from the `source` string (terraform_source.py:256-263, 288-294)

docs/grounding.md:349 asserts 'a private-address host is permitted only when it exactly matches a credentialed hostname' — a guarantee the code does not enforce for public DNS names resolving to private addresses
no `socket.getaddrinfo`/`gethostbyname` resolved-IP filtering exists (search for `gethostbyname` and `169.254` returned no matches)
advisory.finding: probe_source's SSRF/target policy is name-based only: `_valid_host`/`_is_private_host` reject literal IPs and private-TLD names but never check the address the hostname RESOLVES to, so a public-looking hostname from a repo `source` that resolves (via DNS) to a link-local/loopback/private address (e.g. 169.254.169.254, 127.0.0.1, 10.x) passes all filters and receives a credentialed outbound HTTPS probe.
scenarios: A pull request adds a Terraform `module` block with `source = "metadata.attacker.com/ns/name/sys"` where that host resolves to 169.254.169.254; probe_source issues an HTTPS GET to it from the review host, enabling cloud-metadata / internal-service SSRF.
An attacker-controlled DNS name resolving to 127.0.0.1 or an internal 10.x service is probed, and 2xx/timing behavior leaks reachability of internal endpoints.
advisory.suggested_fix: Before probing, resolve the host via socket.getaddrinfo and reject when any resolved IP is private/loopback/link-local/reserved (ipaddress.is_private/is_loopback/is_link_local/is_reserved), unless the host exactly matches a credentialed hostname per the documented policy; ideally pin the connection to the validated IP to avoid a TOCTOU rebind between the check and the urllib request.
